explanation: To retrieve both sides of a many-to-many relationship, each main table must be joined to the associative table using its own matching key. That is why Employees joins to Enrollments on employee_id and Courses joins to Enrollments on course_id.

options.text: Join Employees to Enrollments on employee_id, then join Courses to Enrollments on course_id.
Join Employees directly to Courses on employee_id = course_id.
Join Employees to Courses once, then join Enrollments only if no rows are found.
Use UNION to combine employee names and course names into one list.

prompt: A company stores training assignments in three tables: Employees(employee_id, employee_name), Courses(course_id, course_name), and Enrollments(employee_id, course_id). Which query pattern correctly returns each employee name with the courses they are enrolled in?
